what_it_is.prose: Thales is a French multinational with a multi-decade Indian footprint across defence, aerospace, identity/security and avionics. It operates two JVs in India: BEL-Thales Systems Limited (radars, formed 2014) and a strategic partnership with BDL for missiles. In October 2025 India signed a $468M / £350M deal with Thales UK for Starstreak/LMM (Martlet) MANPADS — the largest UK-India defence deal to date. Thales and BEL announced a MANPADS initial-supply agreement in February 2025. Thales delivers RBE2 radar components (with BEL supplying transmit-receive modules) for India's 36 Rafale fighters; has signed an 11-year avionics maintenance contract with IndiGo (Sep 2025); is developing the PHAROS fire-control radar with BEL; supplies HELIXVIEW airport scanners; and is rolling out face-as-boarding-pass at Indian airports.

faq.question: What is Thales's biggest India defence contract?
faq.answer: Thales UK's $468 million (£350 million) deal for the Lightweight Multirole Missile (LMM / Martlet) MANPADS, signed on 9 October 2025 during PM Modi's summit with UK PM Starmer, is the largest UK-India defence deal on record and Thales's largest single Indian missile order.

faq.question: What joint ventures does Thales have in India?
faq.answer: Thales has two Indian JVs: BEL-Thales Systems Limited (BTSL, formed 2014, co-producing radars including the PHAROS fire-control radar), and a strategic partnership with Bharat Dynamics Limited (BDL) for initial supply and eventual co-production of MANPADS such as the LMM/Martlet, formalised in February 2025.

faq.question: Does Thales supply components for India's Rafale fighters?
faq.answer: Yes. Thales is the OEM of the RBE2 AESA radar on the Dassault Rafale operated by the Indian Air Force (36 aircraft). Under Make-in-India offsets, BEL supplies transmit-receive modules to Thales for the RBE2, and Thales has also awarded SFO Technologies an RBE2 radar wired-structures contract (Dec 2025).
